findings.body:
**Return a JSON error for malformed launchd templates.**

If a preview plist has truncated XML, `plistlib.loads()` can raise `ExpatError`. Line 1013 does not catch it. `--json preview` then prints a traceback to stderr and produces no JSON error on stdout. The config and systemd preview files have already been written. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/3.11/Lib/plistlib.py))

Convert `ExpatError` to a `ValueError` that identifies the template. This uses the existing exit-1 handler and leaves valid templates unchanged. As per coding guidelines, “In machine mode (`--json`) stderr stays empty.”
findings.title: Return a JSON error for malformed launchd templates.

findings.body:
**Restore the original branch attachment on switch failure.**

Line 414 allows the deployment checkout to be on `main`. If checkout succeeds but the `switch-render` audit fails, Line 881 restores the previous commit with `--detach`. The config comes back, but HEAD is no longer attached to `main`. ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-checkout?utm_source=openai))

Record the original symbolic ref before switching. During recovery, restore that branch if it still names the saved commit. Preserve detached HEAD for an originally detached checkout and for a successful forward switch.
findings.title: Restore the original branch attachment on switch failure.

findings.body:
**Protect the first live config write with switch recovery.**

If `git restore` replaces the live config and the parent receives an interrupt before the call returns, Line 856 has not entered the recovery block. HEAD stays on the prior commit, but the live file loses its host overrides. The operator must recover them from the saved backup. By default, `git restore` takes the worktree contents from the index. ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-restore?utm_source=openai))

Enter the recovery block before this call. If HEAD has not moved, reinstall `current` without checking out another commit. Keep the restore before checkout on the successful path.
findings.title: Protect the first live config write with switch recovery.

findings.body:
**Recognize `ExecStart` directives with whitespace before `=`.**

A valid `Type=oneshot` template can contain both `ExecStart=...` and `ExecStart = ...`. Lines 465 and 650 count only the first directive. The Node render replaces it and leaves the second command in the unit. Systemd recognizes both directives. ([github.com](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/main/man/systemd.syntax.xml?utm_source=openai))

Use one directive parser for validation, replacement, and `exec_start` reporting. Reject two effective `ExecStart` directives and continue to accept a single directive.
findings.title: Recognize `ExecStart` directives with whitespace before `=`.
